stops.stop: The Yonne, France, the drop of Team Bruce
stops.date_confidence: attested: the night of 13 into 14 August 1944 (CENTCOM Citadel; European Center of Military History). The coordinate is a departmental centroid; the exact drop zone is not given in any reachable source. The research pool's claim that the sector was liberated in the second week of September conflicts with the record, Sens falling 21 August and Auxerre 24 August.

stops.stop: Jaevsjoen, Norway, the ice at the opening of Operation Rype
stops.date_confidence: attested: 24 March 1945. Coordinates from Wikidata Q6977515 for the lake straddling Snaasa and Aare; the figures circulating in the research pool pointed at Snaasa village, some 40 km northwest. Personnel counts conflict: 35 designed and 15 arrived (HistoryNet) against 31 expected and 12 arrived (secondary summaries). The journey follows the traceable figures.

stops.stop: Rock Point, Maryland, last seen at a quarter past seven
stops.date_confidence: attested: about 7:15 p.m. on 27 April 1996 (Washington Post, 7 May 1996). Coordinates are the corrected position of Rock Point, 38 deg 16 min 19 sec N, 76 deg 50 min 27 sec W; figures circulating in the research pool put the place seventeen kilometers inland and off the river entirely.

stops.stop: The Wicomico River, the body on the marsh bank
stops.date_confidence: attested: canoe found beached 28 April, body recovered 6 May 1996, ruling issued 11 May. The length of the search is reported inconsistently: nine days from the last sighting on 27 April, eight from the finding of the canoe on 28 April. Both figures appear in the sources and neither is wrong.

stops.stop: Arlington National Cemetery, Section 59, Grave 655
stops.date_confidence: attested: buried with military honors 13 May 1996, Section 59, Grave 655 (Arlington burial records; Find a Grave memorial 5898372). The absence of any monument elsewhere is an inference from a failed search plus the published criteria of the CIA Memorial Wall, and is carried as reconstruction.
